Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

big mouth noun

also big-mouth!, loudmouth, you brazen thing!, cheeky, he was always a big-mouth, have a sharp tongue, talkative

classical

Cic. Sen. 55: senectūs est nātūrā loquācior (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 158

loquāx, loquācis

Declension on Wiktionary

talkative, a chatterbox

Other words

  • ōs dūrum! — you brazen face! the cheek of it!

    also used · classical · Ter. Eun. 4.7.36 (Lewis & Short s.v. ōs); Traupman 94

    (vōx cōmica: Ter.)

    Traupman’s word for “big-mouth!”, but in Latin it is cheek rather than talk: ōs, the face, is impudence, and dūrum, hard, unblushing (so ōs dūrissimum, a very brazen man, Cic. Quinct. 77).

  • dūrae buccae esse — have a sharp tongue, be a big mouth

    also used · post-classical · Petr. 43.3: dūrae buccae fuit, linguōsus (Lewis & Short s.v. bucca); Traupman 94

    (vōx sermōnis vulgāris: Petr.)

    A genitive of quality: “he was of a hard cheek”.

  • clāmātor, clāmātōris m. — a bawler, a loudmouth

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Traupman 155 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Lewis & Short: of a noisy speaker in oratory.

Examples

  • Semper dūrae buccae fuit.

    He was always a big-mouth.Traupman 94
